title: Surface and Bulk Leakage Current Flow

key_findings.detail:
At least six leakage current pathways have been identified in a standard glass-encapsulant-cell-backsheet module stack, with glass surface conduction dominant at high humidity:

1. Along the front glass surface and through the glass/encapsulant bulk
2. Through the front glass bulk laterally, then through the encapsulant
3. Along the glass/encapsulant interface, then through the encapsulant
4. Through the encapsulant bulk only
5. Along the encapsulant/backsheet interface, then through the encapsulant
6. Along the backsheet surface and through the backsheet/encapsulant

Pathway 1 (glass surface) dominates at realistic humidity levels because glass surface resistivity drops far more steeply with humidity than encapsulant bulk resistivity:
- [[papers/MDPI-36-1297-2-s2.0-86000085439-2023-J-Potential Induced Degradation in Photovoltaic Modules: A Review of the Latest Research and Developme.pdf#page=4|Badran & Dhimish (2023), p.4]]

Leakage current through glass is **almost exclusively ionic** (Na⁺ ions); the polymer (EVA, POE) shows primarily ionic conduction with some electronic contribution:[^slc_ionic]

- Glass resistance at 23°C, 50% RH: ~$1.0 \times 10^{10}$ to $1.1 \times 10^{11}$ Ω
- EVA resistance: ~$1.7 \times 10^{14}$ Ω
- **Glass surface resistivity activation energy:** 99 ± 14 kJ/mol (strong humidity dependence)
- **EVA volumetric resistivity activation energy:** 102 ± 6 kJ/mol
- **POE volumetric resistivity activation energy:** 84 ± 6 kJ/mol

- [[papers/Wiley-136-1282-2-s2.0-85148423463-2023-J-Electrochemical mechanisms of leakage-current in photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=2|Vogt et al. (2023), p.2]]

key_findings.detail:
- **Dry module steady-state leakage current:** ~10 nA
- **Wet module leakage current:** ~35× higher than dry
- EVA resistivity is two orders of magnitude higher than glass resistivity (10¹⁴ vs. 10¹² Ω·cm)
- Glass surface resistance becomes the critical limiting factor at high humidity
- [[papers/IEEE-171-2371-2-s2.0-85099585463-2020-C-Modeling of Leakage Currents in c-Si PV Modules and Investigation of their Arrhenius Behavior.pdf#page=2|Spataru et al. (2020), p.2]]

key_findings.claim: Three-Stage Current Transient Under Voltage Application
key_findings.detail:
When system voltage is applied, the leakage current exhibits three temporal stages:

1. **0–6 seconds:** Displacement (capacitive) current dominates; 15–20× larger than steady-state conduction current
2. **6–10 seconds:** Linear voltage ramp; displacement current continues
3. **After 10 seconds:** Conduction current dominates at steady state; ~35 nA/m² at 1000 V

- [[papers/IEEE-183-2385-2-s2.0-85099531570-2020-C-Theoretical insight into leakage current of solar module under high system voltage.pdf#page=2|Zhao et al. (2020), p.2]]

Leakage current is not uniform across the module area; it decreases from frame edge toward module center:

- **Dry conditions (40°C):** Current density nearly constant (~0.14 nA/cm²) regardless of distance from frame because glass surface resistance dominates
- **Wet moderate humidity (75% RH, saturated EVA):** Current density varies 10-fold from frame edge to cell center, depending on whether the surface is soiled or clean
- **Fully wet (90% RH):** Current density reaches ~19 nA/cm² maximum, relatively flat distribution

- [[papers/AIP-114-2645-2-s2.0-85071569696-2019-C-Influence of soiling and moisture ingress on long term PID susceptibility of photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=3|Richter et al. (2019), p.3]]

A voltage of at least **~10 V** must drop across the SiNx ARC layer to initiate significant PID. This corresponds to leakage current densities of **10–30 nA/cm²**. Soiling can push cells near frame edges over this threshold even at moderate system voltages:
- [[papers/AIP-114-2645-2-s2.0-85071569696-2019-C-Influence of soiling and moisture ingress on long term PID susceptibility of photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=2|Richter et al. (2019), p.2]]

A one-to-one relationship exists between **total charge transferred to the active cell area** and **power loss**. Power loss is directly proportional to accumulated Na⁺ dose. At higher voltages (−2000 to −3000 V), degradation saturates because $Q = CV$ limits maximum Na⁺ accumulation:[^slc_charge]
- [[papers/IOP-44-3195-2-s2.0-85039161903-2017-J-Quantitative analysis of relationship between leakage current and power loss of multi-crystalline si.pdf#page=2|Kawamura et al. (2017), p.2]]

key_findings.detail:
Applying hydrophobic PTFE tape at module edges breaks the surface conduction pathway and reduced power loss from **29% to 15–17%** under PID stress. Complete elimination requires non-conductive barriers such as Corning Willow Glass:
- [[papers/SPIE-139-3142-2-s2.0-85056841926-2018-C-Addressing potential-induced degradation of field-installed PV modules by reducing surface conductiv.pdf#page=3|Hacke et al. (2018), p.3]]
